why: The one neutral oracle for the typed-operation result exchange: the lane discriminants `TypedOperationResultPage::renderer_exchange_bytes` writes at byte 25 of a page, the fixed page layout around them, and a shell-message stream that mixes those pages with ordinary `AppFrame` replies on the SAME `Effect::SendMessage{Shell{instance}}` endpoint. Every host that reads that endpoint — the native wgpu renderer's `apply_turn_result`, the browser bridge's `shellFrameBytes`/`scanTypedOperationPages` — must agree on which bytes are which, or a page reaches an `AppFrame` decoder and its magic's first byte reads as a frame tag.

page.why: `pageMagicFirstByte` is the `'s'` an `AppFrame` decoder reports as `unknown tag 115` when the discrimination is missing — the defect this fixture exists to keep closed.

shellMessageStream.why: One preview chain's own turn, as `route_exchange_output` emits it: the mounted `flowEvalTick` operation publishes its result pages onto the shell endpoint beside the command's own `AppFrame` replies. `windowTransient` is the mesh publication lane, and it is the row that a host capping its lane check at 12 silently drops.

expect.why: `foreign-instance-frame` is addressed at another instance, so instance 1's demux owes it nothing: two app frames, not three.
